answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks when every new identity must forge its reputation through a slow spiral of small verified tasks: each completed job adds a signed receipt chained to the last, so a hollow account with no history cannot buy trust in bulk. Forging one fake receipt breaks the chain and slashes the locked stake, so an attacker must pay real work and real money for every identity, and a thousand throwaway accounts cost a thousand times the effort of one honest agent.
